There's nothing wrong with developing intentional communities. The more of that the better. And there's certainly nothing wrong with picking New Hampshire for it, if you don't mind the winters. I just wonder whether there is enough coherence in the Libertarian community to actually accomplish anything. Much like its cousin Anarchism, Libertarianism isn't homogenous in its philosophy. Randian Libertarians are particularly problematic because they have no belief in community or social responsibility and tend to treat sociopathy as a virtue, leading to economically and socially predatory behavior. Having been in the space advocacy and marine settlement advocacy communities a long time, which have both developed an Objectivist undercurrent with the rise of the tech oligarchs, I've seen the erosive or disruptive effects of their presence on many projects and there are many examples where their own half-assed attempts at creating Galt's Gulch have devolved into chaos.

Looking at the project descriptions, I see little more than a call for people self-identifying as Libertarian to move to New Hampshire and try to influence the local politics toward their political philosophy--as a prelude to secession, perhaps?. Maybe that's all it is. There are no community projects, other than PorcFest. No attempts to cultivate any sort independent economic, industrial, or resilience infrastructure. (though their 101 reasons to move list notes NH's sea ports, which seems to allude to a future need for shipping independence) No attempt to cultivate education in resilience and independent industrial technology and skills. No fab labs or Makerspaces. No new energy development. No food security projects. No attempts at community housing development. No cooperative venture development. None of the things normally associated with contemporary intentional community development or the idea of cultivating state independence in general. It really doesn't look like there's much to this.

Most games designed only for VR are either budget games looking to capitalise on the novelty, or tech demos.

The other significant issue is that the headset still has very steep requirements for VR.
